texts.orig: 1. Set arbitrary deadlines
texts.text: 1. Set arbitrary deadlines

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Deadlines work. Even arbitrary ones.
texts.text: Deadlines work. Even arbitrary ones.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: One of my favorite techniques for getting someone to finish something that’s important but not urgent is to come up with an arbitrary deadline together. I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.
texts.text: One of my favorite techniques for getting someone to finish something that’s important but not urgent is to come up with an arbitrary deadline together. I say to the person, “Let’s come up with an arbitrary deadline!” We both know it’s made up, but there’s a weird gravitational pull once you’ve put a date out there.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It’s important to have the person doing the work pick the deadline so that it’s a date that works for them. You’d be surprised how often it’s very reasonable. And how often they hit it.

texts.orig: 2. Use pen and paper for your to-dos—and rewrite them each morning
texts.text: 2. Use pen and paper for your to-dos—and rewrite them each morning

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Something I’ve learned about myself is that if my to-dos are sitting inside an app on my laptop, the one place I don’t want to look is that app on my laptop. There’s hard work to do there! Let’s check my email and Slack channels for the thousandth time instead.
texts.text: Something I’ve learned about myself is that if my to-dos are sitting inside an app on my laptop, the one place I don’t want to look is that app on my laptop. There’s hard work to do there! Let’s check my email and Slack channels for the thousandth time instead.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: However, when my to-dos are sitting right in front of my face, in a nice notebook I can’t swipe away (and always have with me), I’m much more likely to see the work I need to do, and thus work on the things I should be working on.

texts.orig: 3. Say no to stuff you’ve said yes to
texts.text: 3. Say no to stuff you’ve said yes to

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In the previous post, I shared a tactic for knowing when to say no: ask yourself, would I say yes if it were tomorrow? Well, often we still say yes, and today is now almost tomorrow. And you’re wishing you didn’t say yes.
texts.text: In the previous post, I shared a tactic for knowing when to say no: ask yourself, would I say yes if it were tomorrow? Well, often we still say yes, and today is now almost tomorrow. And you’re wishing you didn’t say yes.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Here’s the good news: often you can still get out of it, without much issue. This will save you a bunch of time and stress, and it’s almost always not a big deal to that person. It just takes crafting the right message to that person.
texts.text: Here’s the good news: often you can still get out of it, without much issue. This will save you a bunch of time and stress, and it’s almost always not a big deal to that person. It just takes crafting the right message to that person.
